doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Growing up in Wyomissing and hearing harmony by ear
summary: She came from a non-show-business family in Wyomissing, PA, played popular songs by ear and could hear harmony.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Would you say that music chose you as opposed to the other way around?

Yeah. I had no way I would be doing anything. My parents were not in show business. I was — actually I’m from Wyomissing, Pennsylvania. Do you recognize that word? Well if you look up Taylor Swift you’ll find out that’s where she’s from.
Wow. You have a connection there.

Well do you recall any — nowadays I would use the word “epiphany.” Back then it might have like AHA!, like an AHA! moment either from recordings or the radio or just something that really reached inside and grabbed you at a young age?

I was always waiting for the next song that was going to be popular, and that’s when they were songs. Like “Slow Boat to China.” Things like that coming in on the radio, and I’d just sit down and play it because I could play by ear, I read music too, but I could play most of what I heard.
Did you hear bass notes? That sounds like a silly question but when I learn a song off a recording or something, the first thing I do is try to figure out the bass notes.
Yeah. But I didn’t think of them because I didn’t even know the word, but I did hear harmony. And don’t ask me how, that’s just a gift that I have that I cannot explain.
